rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents and occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue for civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports that do not recommend rents, affordable-housing rent/income limit products, and market research for financing, appraisal, or software development research/testing/training.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; damages, injunctive relief, restitution; attorney's fees to prevailing plaintiff
rules.effective_date_note: Ordinance 7,992-N.S. text provided states no effective date (passed to print Nov 18, 2025; adopted Dec 2, 2025 agenda). 2026-03-01 is the date reported for the ordinance text; a law-firm alert says January 2026.
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: March 1, 2026 (ordinance text, per reports) vs. January 2026 (Morgan Lewis alert, D002/D037). The provided official document does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or lease decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
citation_aliases: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties; owner move-back agreements (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation, actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees, injunctive relief.
rules.effective_date_note: Only the Council passage date (April 14, 2020) is given; used as effective date.

unverifiable_exemptions: existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (just cause, notices, relocation assistance)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units can be evicted only for just cause. Nonpayment eviction requires debt of at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent; no eviction for refusing a new fixed-term lease; termination notices must refer to the Rent Board and be filed with it within three business days. Owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions require relocation assistance ($19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households in 2026).
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value
rules.key_value: Just cause for nearly all units; nonpayment only if debt ≥ 1 month HUD FMR; 2026 relocation $19,413 + $6,471
rules.exemptions: Golden duplexes, owner-shared kitchen/bath units, certain ADU properties, university housing, nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB passed in November 2024 election; Notice of Tenant Rights applies to tenancies from 2024-12-20; 2026 relocation amounts effective 2026-01-01.

unverifiable_exemptions: unit shared with landlord who lived there first

rules.review_note: Chapter 13.76 is not named in the just-cause pages; inferred from D008 (BMC 13.76.110A) and cross-reference to BMC 13.76.130 in D003.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – rent stabilization and Annual General Adjustment (max 5%)
rules.requirement: Fully covered units (most multifamily buildings built before 1980, older single-family tenancies) have a rent ceiling raised yearly by the Annual General Adjustment, 65% of Bay Area CPI and never more than 5%. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, usable no earlier than January 1, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%
rules.exemptions: Partially covered and exempt units (new construction with CO after 1980, most condos, single-family tenancies from 1996) have no rent ceiling.
rules.interaction: State Costa-Hawkins Act limits local rent control on newer buildings and single-family homes/condos; local rent control governs covered units instead of the state Tenant Protection Act cap.
rules.effective_date_note: 5% cap from Measure BB (November 2024); 2026 AGA order effective 2026-01-01.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes with tenancies begun before 1996 are covered regardless of year

rules.conflict_note: Cutoff described as 'built before 1980' (D006, D009 table) vs. 'CO after June 1980' (D009); exact boundary ambiguous.
rules.review_note: Section 13.76.110A is cited in D008 for AGA rules.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, prorated if the tenant moves out earlier.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year
rules.interaction: Operates alongside the state deposit cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
rules.review_note: Code section not stated in the documents; ch. 13.76 inferred as the Rent Ordinance chapter.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable existing-tenancy fees
rules.requirement: Owners charging a fee for a credit report and application processing must give applicants, before taking the fee, a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the maximum fee cap under Civil Code 1950.6(b) ($68.96 for 2026). Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add/replace a roommate.
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.key_value: Fee rights and cap disclosure before fee; no non-refundable renewal/roommate fees
